_comment2: The dragon wounds Flood. Hannah's scream triggers audio. Hannah casts her
_comment3: ultimate spell, killing the dragon. Flood still dies. Hannah explains the cost.

speaker: Narrator
text: The dragon moves faster than anything that size has a right to. The strike is not aimed at the party — it is aimed at Flood, specifically, deliberately, as though it has known her name from the start.

speaker: Flood
text: Gh—

speaker: Narrator
text: Flood hits the ground. She does not get up.

speaker: Hannah
text: FLOOD—!

speaker: Narrator
text: Hannah does not pause. She does not speak. She does not look at the dragon as though it is a threat — she looks at it as though it has already lost and simply hasn't been told yet.

speaker: Narrator
text: The light that comes from her hands is not the light of a spell. It is older than that. It fills the chamber like water fills a drowning thing — completely, and from every direction at once.

speaker: Narrator
text: The dragon falls.

speaker: Narrator
text: The silence afterward is the loudest thing any of them have ever heard.

speaker: Narrator
text: Javin reaches Flood first. The wound is not survivable. That much is clear before anyone speaks.

speaker: Flood
text: Don't.

speaker: Flood
text: Don't apologise. I know what you're going to say and I don't want it.

speaker: Javin
text: Flood—

speaker: Flood
text: I said don't.

speaker: Flood
text: Tell me it mattered. That's all. Just tell me it mattered.

speaker: Javin
text: It mattered.

speaker: Flood
text: Good.

speaker: Narrator
text: Hannah has not moved. When she finally speaks, her voice is steady in the way that things are steady after they have already broken.

speaker: Hannah
text: If I were to cast a spell that strong again... it would kill me.

speaker: Hannah
text: I want you to know that. So you know what it cost. So it isn't just something that happened.

speaker: Javin
text: Hannah...

speaker: Hannah
text: She was worth it. Don't let anyone tell you she wasn't.
